name: China
intro: It's 1949. You've just won a civil war after a century of humiliation. Your country is broken, illiterate, and surrounded: Americans in Japan and Korea, Chiang on Taiwan, the Soviets as ally-but-also-overlord. Stalin doesn't fully trust you. You want China to stand up. Choose whose shadow to stand in — or none.

nodes.title: Lean to One Side
nodes.situation: Stalin offers a treaty with strings (Port Arthur, Mongolia). The US hints at recognition if you stay independent.

effects.text: $300M loan and 10,000 advisors, Soviet-model industry
effects.insight: your economy is built on their blueprint, which you'll later reject

effects.text: Recognition dies; 22 years of no contact
effects.insight: "Who lost China?" poisons US politics

effects.text: Chiang survives on US aid
effects.insight: Taiwan's fate is now a superpower issue

effects.text: You recognize Ho Chi Minh first; Vietnam becomes your revolutionary client
effects.insight: you'll fight him in 1979

effects.text: You concede Mongolia's independence
effects.insight: a price paid for the treaty that Chinese nationalists still resent.

effects.text: Acheson's "let the dust settle" wins; US recognition by 1951
effects.insight: Korea then plays very differently

effects.text: Stalin calls you a "Titoist," cuts aid
effects.insight: you're isolated but free

effects.text: Without Soviet blueprints, you improvise
effects.insight: a peasant-centered model (Mao's real instinct) emerges a decade early

effects.text: US, no longer seeing you as Soviet proxy, pressures Chiang to negotiate
effects.insight: a One-China deal in the 1950s becomes conceivable

effects.text: Japan trades with you by 1952
effects.insight: the East Asian economy integrates 20 years early.

effects.text: McCarthy's Republicans block any deal
effects.insight: you're rebuffed and humiliated

effects.text: Stalin, enraged, backs a rival faction (Gao Gang)
effects.insight: your party splits

effects.text: Kim, distrusting you, relies entirely on Stalin
effects.insight: the Korean War proceeds without your buffer role

effects.text: Rebuffed, you swing hard left
effects.insight: the Great Leap comes early

effects.text: British colony becomes your only window
effects.insight: a role it plays till 1997 anyway.

nodes.title: Cross the Yalu
nodes.situation: UN forces approach your border. Stalin promises air cover, then hedges. Your generals say the army is exhausted.

effects.text: You push the UN back, then stall
effects.insight: 180,000 Chinese dead for a stalemate

effects.text: 7th Fleet permanently guards Taiwan
effects.insight: the price of Korea

effects.text: "China stood up"
effects.insight: legitimacy surge, mass mobilization, purges of "counter-revolutionaries" (700,000+ killed)

effects.text: Stalin's late air cover confirms he'll use you
effects.insight: the seed of the split

effects.text: China becomes the "Yellow Peril" of US politics for two decades
effects.insight: no trade, no seat at the UN.

effects.text: Kim's regime collapses; a US-allied unified Korea sits on your border
effects.insight: the encirclement you feared

effects.text: Stalin treats you as unreliable; aid shrinks
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: Nationalist critics ask what the revolution was for
effects.insight: Mao purges them anyway

effects.text: Without Korea, the US fleet doesn't deploy
effects.insight: you invade Taiwan in 1951 and win

effects.text: Japan hosts US nukes aimed at you
effects.insight: the shield gets closer.

effects.text: Bombing Kyushu bases brings Japan into the war
effects.insight: a rearmed Japan by 1952

effects.text: Truman authorizes nuclear strikes on Manchurian staging areas
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

chance.successText: A nuclear weapon is used. The crisis has crossed a threshold; leaders now face the danger of a wider exchange.
chance.failureText: Leaders stop short of nuclear use in this run. The confrontation still damages trust and raises the risk of another crisis.

effects.text: Stalin, terrified of being dragged in, cuts you loose
effects.insight: you're alone

effects.text: US carrier strikes hit your coast; industry collapses
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The war becomes the regime's whole identity
effects.insight: a North Korea-style garrison state.

nodes.title: Let a Hundred Flowers Bloom
nodes.situation: Khrushchev has denounced Stalin. Intellectuals want to criticize the party. Moscow's model is delivering slow growth. Mao is impatient.

effects.text: Backyard furnaces and communes
effects.insight: 30–45 million die in the famine 1959–61

effects.text: Khrushchev mocks the Leap; you call him a revisionist
effects.insight: the split becomes ideological

effects.text: Mao retreats from daily rule; Liu Shaoqi and Deng repair the economy
effects.insight: Mao's revenge becomes the Cultural Revolution

effects.text: The 1959 Tibetan uprising, fed by Leap-era coercion, is crushed; the Dalai Lama flees to India
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Sheltering the Dalai Lama poisons Sino-Indian ties
effects.insight: the 1962 war is now on the calendar.

effects.text: Heavy industry grows 8%/yr on Soviet plans
effects.insight: no famine, no Leap

effects.text: Alliance holds through the 1960s
effects.insight: the split, if it comes, is later and milder

effects.text: Mao's radicals are marginalized; a technocratic party emerges
effects.insight: the Cultural Revolution never happens

effects.text: A stable Sino-Soviet bloc is more frightening
effects.insight: the US spends more on Asia, less on Vietnam adventures (nothing to "roll back")

effects.text: Prosperous mainland tempts Taiwan's business class
effects.insight: cross-strait contact begins in the 1970s.

choices.summary: Hundred Flowers For Real — Open Debate

effects.text: Criticism overwhelms the party within months; Mao either reverses (historically he did, purging 500,000 as "rightists") or loses control
effects.insight: Partners judge a commitment by what it costs you to keep it. A changed commitment reshapes their choices.

effects.text: A reformist intellectual wing survives
effects.insight: China's 1980s arrive in the 1960s

effects.text: Khrushchev cites you as proof of thaw
effects.insight: Eastern Europe's reformers are emboldened

effects.text: Hungary-style unrest spreads to Guangzhou students
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Chiang loses the "free China" monopoly; Western opinion shifts toward you.
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

nodes.title: Himalaya
nodes.situation: India has pushed border posts into disputed territory ("Forward Policy"). Nehru refuses to negotiate. The USSR sells India MiGs. Cuba is in crisis; the world is distracted.

effects.text: You rout Indian forces in a month, then withdraw unilaterally
effects.insight: a message, not a conquest

effects.text: Nehru is broken; India militarizes and starts its nuclear program
effects.insight: the bomb comes in 1974

effects.text: Pakistan becomes your ally
effects.insight: the "all-weather friendship" starts here

effects.text: Khrushchev supports India during the Cuban crisis
effects.insight: proof to you the alliance is dead

effects.text: The US airlifts arms to India
effects.insight: briefly, until Pakistan complains.

choices.label: Negotiate — Swap Aksai Chin for Arunachal
choices.summary: Negotiate — Swap Aksai Chin for Arunachal

effects.text: Nehru accepts the swap (his 1960 position was close)
effects.insight: the border is settled forever

effects.text: Pakistan, denied a Chinese patron, leans fully on the US
effects.insight: no Sino-Pak axis, no nuclear help later

effects.text: A quiet border reduces Tibetan insurgency support from India
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Khrushchev claims credit
effects.insight: the alliance limps on

effects.text: A China–India understanding alarms the US
effects.insight: the "Asian giants" framing appears in the 1960s, not the 2000s.

effects.text: You occupy to the Brahmaputra; India's northeast becomes an insurgent zone
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: India joins the US in a formal treaty by 1964
effects.insight: nonalignment dies

effects.text: The USSR arms India massively
effects.insight: you now have hostile superpowers on both flanks

effects.text: Pakistan attacks Kashmir opportunistically in 1963
effects.insight: a two-front war for India

effects.text: The US considers nuclear guarantees for India
effects.insight: Asia goes nuclear a decade early.

nodes.title: Bombard the Headquarters
nodes.situation: Mao, sidelined since the famine, calls students to purge "capitalist roaders." Liu Shaoqi and Deng control the party machine. The Vietnam War rages on your border.

effects.text: Red Guards destroy the party, universities close for years, 1–2 million die
effects.insight: a decade lost

effects.text: 1967 riots and bombs
effects.insight: Britain nearly loses the colony

effects.text: You still send 320,000 troops to North Vietnam
effects.insight: chaos at home, war abroad

effects.text: Paranoia peaks in the 1969 border war with the USSR
effects.insight: 2,000 dead

effects.text: A China at war with itself and Moscow is a China ready for Nixon
effects.insight: the opening's precondition.

choices.label: Mao Retires — Liu and Deng Rule
choices.summary: Mao Retires — Liu and Deng Rule

effects.text: Pragmatic reforms of 1962–65 continue
effects.insight: China's Deng era starts in 1966

effects.text: A rational China negotiates the border; the split freezes rather than boils
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: Aid to Vietnam is conditioned on negotiation
effects.insight: the war ends sooner

effects.text: No Sino-Soviet war, less reason for Nixon's opening
effects.insight: but trade begins by 1970 via Japan

effects.text: Prosperity draws Taiwan's businesses; reunification talks in the 1980s.
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

choices.label: Cultural Revolution Plus War With the USSR
choices.summary: Cultural Revolution Plus War With the USSR

effects.text: Border clashes become full war; Soviet forces bomb Manchuria
effects.insight: you fight with militia and slogans

effects.text: The Politburo debates nuclear strikes on your bomb sites (this was real in 1969)
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

effects.text: Nixon warns Moscow off
effects.insight: the US becomes your de facto protector

effects.text: The army takes over from Red Guards; a military dictatorship under Lin Biao
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: Vietnam sides with Moscow; you're at war on two fronts.
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

nodes.title: The Handshake
nodes.situation: Nixon wants to visit. Lin Biao is dead in a mysterious plane crash. The Soviets have a million troops on your border. Zhou Enlai says the Americans can be used; Mao's wife says it's betrayal.

effects.text: The Shanghai Communiqué; UN seat won; Taiwan expelled
effects.insight: you're a great power again

effects.text: Brezhnev, fearing US–China encirclement, rushes to sign SALT
effects.insight: your leverage on both

effects.text: Japan normalizes relations within months
effects.insight: trade explodes

effects.text: Pakistan, your matchmaker, is rewarded with US silence over Bangladesh atrocities
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: The door is open; when Deng wins in 1978 there's someone to trade with.
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: Radicals dominate; Deng never returns from exile
effects.insight: reform is delayed a decade or more

effects.text: Without a US–China axis, the Soviets don't need SALT
effects.insight: the arms race runs hotter

effects.text: Nixon settles for détente with Moscow alone
effects.insight: the US–Soviet condominium Europeans feared

effects.text: Taiwan keeps its UN seat into the 1980s
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Vietnam stays loyal to you
effects.insight: no 1979 war, but no reform either.

choices.label: Play Both — Also Reconcile With Moscow
choices.summary: Play Both — Also Reconcile With Moscow

effects.text: Border settlement and resumed trade
effects.insight: the split heals into rivalry

effects.text: Kissinger fears a "united front"
effects.insight: the US gives you more to keep you

effects.text: Japan hedges
effects.insight: slower normalization

effects.text: Both patrons united, Vietnam wins in 1973
effects.insight: Partners judge a commitment by what it costs you to keep it. A changed commitment reshapes their choices.

effects.text: India, losing its Soviet counterweight to you, tests its bomb in 1972 and courts the US.

nodes.title: Reform and Opening
nodes.situation: Mao is dead. Deng has outmaneuvered the Gang of Four. Vietnam has invaded Cambodia, your ally. The economy is at famine levels in parts of the countryside.
